A problem only exists when there is a difference between the current state and the end state. If there is no difference, there is no problem.

Statements about the nature of reality must be supported by evidence in order to have a practical impact on my life. If the way things really are is different than we can prove with evidence, then it does not matter because the current state of not knowing is practically indifferent from the goal state of "knowing".

Here's an example: Suppose I am standing in the rain. It makes no difference for me to learn that its not really raining. I still want an umbrella.

Philosophy departments the world round rack their brains on the problem of external world skepticism. Except, the problem doesn't exist - there is no difference between where they are and where they hope to be.

Many of the assertions you are making suffer from this deeply rooted flaw.

For instance, If we are never born as you say and never die as you suggest, then it doesn't matter because I have no evidence to support it and it has no practical value for my life.

If my goal is to seek the truth and behave in ways that are logically consistent with reality, then believing something for which I have no evidence, and then behaving as if it's true, is an unreliable means of achieving my goal.

The free will / determinism debate has the same problem. We seem free, and can decide among ourselves whether we will be held accountable for our decisions. The facts in this case do not require me to live in a society that does not hold people accountable for their good and bad decisions. I want to be accountable because I make damn good decisions, and my hard work and the fruits of my labor are mine alone.

In saying that, the scientific method has some major flaws despite being a useful system.

1. Confirmation Bias/Regression to the Mean/Group Think.

This means we're likely to ignore things when they don't fit our world theory. Reseachers and Test-givers are not immune to this and have time and time again created flawed results which we unknowningly accept. We even use these logicaly fallacies when setting the parameters for tests and studies meaning we can make up/narrow our mind on what we believe before we ever start testing.

2. Lack Of Ability To Prove Personal Experiences.

While commonly believed that it is less likely that the experience of one is true when compared to the experience of many, it does not mean that the one is wrong. This includes those who have any kind of credentials experiencing something together. Logical fallacies creep into the understanding of how science works meaning Bandwagon, Appeal to Authority, and Circular Reasoning amongst many more are all prevelant in the common defense of scientific study. This flaw in science is one of the fundamental reasons it is commonly at odds with Religion which is in practice a personal, not group, belief system. Let us not forget Psychology had this exact same thing holding it back in our culture until a group of (Surprise! Surprise!) old, white men finally found a system of measuring it they were OK with. Think about that, we held back an entire immensely important field of science just because the major science community considered a psuedo-science. This is the nature of humankind and it's not a new thing.

3. Logical Positivism Is An Unproven Philosphy Ingrained In The Understanding of Science.

The idea that any given 'scientific' study is a font of truth is simply not the case. A great quote that summarizes my point, "One of the foundational principles of science since Karl Popper is that of falsifiability. In order for something to be valid scientifically, it must be possible to test it and prove it false. How is the principle of falsifiability falsifiable? It's not. By its own standard, falsifiability, and therefore science, is unscientific. If you do not view science as a source of truth, and instead view it as a methodology for acquiring useful information, these fallacies no longer apply. These are more objections to the philosophical movements Scientism and Logical positivism than to science itself, but many people who think they are advocating "science" are actually advocating logical positivism without knowing it." Science is subject to many, many flaws. Never forget that.

4. Corruption.

Sadly, any science must be done by humans and those humans have all the weaknesses you do. Enough money, power, or influence can ensure a study is done in a certain way or a study is to be given no credit. This means we always have to be aware of this possibility and back up anything we see with a solid, personal study. You might ask, "You mean I have to actually find out something is true for myself without listening to someone else tell me what's true?".

Yes. Yes, you do, little human.
